# vallus

> Self-hosted Playwright test runner with a web dashboard. Teams register their
> existing Playwright or pytest-playwright projects, then schedule, trigger and
> review runs from one place. Every instance runs on the customer's own
> infrastructure: no telemetry, no licence server, no call home. Once installed
> it needs no route to the internet at all.

Made by ExpandIt (Piotr Gajownik), Poland. Proprietary software, distributed in
binary form under its End User Licence Agreement. It is not open source, and a
valid licence key is required to run it.

## What it is for

vallus sits between a test framework and the people who need its results. The
Playwright CLI works for one developer on one machine; vallus turns the same
projects into repeatable workflows that anyone on the team can run on demand, on
a schedule, or from CI, with reports, traces and cross-run history kept locally.

It is built for closed and regulated environments: air-gapped networks, banks,
public institutions, and any deployment where test data and results may not
leave the customer's perimeter.

## Writing

- [Articles](https://vallus.eu/articles/): notes on test automation in closed environments
- [The version you are on is the version you are stuck with](https://vallus.eu/articles/updating-playwright-behind-air-gap/): keeping Playwright current behind an air gap - choosing an upgrade cadence, what breaks when you jump several versions, and making a rollback a path change
- [One tarball is a procedure, twenty is a problem](https://vallus.eu/articles/internal-browser-mirror/): serving Playwright browser archives from your own artifact repository once copying tarballs stops scaling
- [The browsers have to get there somehow](https://vallus.eu/articles/playwright-offline-install/): installing Playwright browsers on a machine with no route to the internet, and carrying several versions so a rollback is not another transfer
- [The tests nobody on the outside will ever see](https://vallus.eu/articles/testing-closed-environments/): automation, reporting and data sovereignty where there is no route to the internet

## Facts worth quoting

- Runs entirely on customer infrastructure; the vendor has no access to test
  data, results, screenshots or traces.
- No telemetry, no licence server, no automatic updates. The licence is a file
  verified locally, so an air-gapped install keeps working.
- Run environment is defined per workflow, each variable declared as a typed value,
  a secret encrypted with the instance key, or a reference resolved from OpenBao or
  HashiCorp Vault at run start. Secrets are never stored in plain text on disk
  between runs. The vault integration is licensed from the Team tier upwards; the
  free tier still encrypts its secrets, it just cannot read an external vault.
- Supports Playwright (Node.js/TypeScript) and pytest-playwright (Python) in the
  same instance, with a separate Playwright version per project.
- Each run executes in its own container when Docker is available, with an image
  per version of the test suite.
- Reports: Playwright HTML per run, Allure when a JRE is present, hosted trace
  viewer, plus run history and cross-run trends stored locally.
- Sizing: roughly 0.4 vCPU and 1.6 GB RAM per concurrent browser. Containers
  need shm_size 2gb, or Chromium crashes on the default 64 MB.
